en: Was slaughtered when my orphan arrived.
My foster father Kyzylsart
Appeared with forty caravans,
And now the honor of sorrowing,
Afflicted Choro has been restored.
If sent ahead, his path is white;
If following behind, his army is countless.
The orphan named in the testament has been found,
And thus the honor of Choro,
Born for grief, has been restored.
Its shaft is sound and its tip is sharp—
The hollow-shafted ornamented spear.
I would increase my feats each time;
Setting hoes in a row,
I would shoot them with my bow.
My arrow would be blunted,
And the faces of the hoes gouged in.
I girded on crimson steel,
And precious Khan Bakai tested me,
Saying, “His strength will suffice for the world.”
Thinking, “He will become someone’s spokesman,”
My dear mother Kanykei
Had me raised with sacred rites.
“The strength of this wrestler is unique,”
Said the saint who led the people,
The collar of the precious robe,
The father of the peoples of the age,
The elder sustained by the sacred spirit,
The sage who had seen many lands—
My uncle Koshoy approved of me.
“Choro’s valor is great and his strength supreme,
Though he is unruly,”
Said heroic Koshoy, approving me when he saw me.
My prowess became known;
“He is a fearsome warrior,” they said,
And when they saw my courage,
Many heroes despaired of their lives.
Wondering whether I was the greater warrior,
Our grandfather Chylaba
Questioned a sorcerer.
When he heard that I was a hero,
He was astonished and amazed.
Lo Ma, the khan of Beijing,
Heard that my valor was exceptional,
And my strength beyond measure;
As the son of Khan Almambet,
My fame became known among the people.
I loaded the great musket,
And only the hardest part
Of the unyielding black earth stopped its shot.
Where I stood became a fortress;
Every enemy I met became a fool.
Life burst from his breastbone.
Such was his prowess:
He played with his ornamented spear,
And every enemy he met crawled away.
He was a hero of surpassing stature,
A panther, a gray-maned warrior—
Such was Külchoro.
Brimming with strength and spreading broad,
Your hero Choro, attended by the sacred spirit,
Your Choro, a hero surpassing the world,
Whose thoroughbred could carry him for six months,
Kinsman of the magnanimous khan—
He too was one of the greatest.
Would the lion-like gray-maned hero stay still?
He summoned Kyzylsart, Seytek, and the Black Giant,
The three of them, to the spectacle;
Would he refrain from wreaking havoc?
He summoned up his former strength.
When the sword Zulpukor
Hung from my arm,
When I wore trousers
That no bullet could pierce,
When I crushed the whole wide world
And held it in my power,
When the hungry blade Achalbars
Swung from my arm,
When I crushed the whole wide world
And took possession of it,
When I brought disaster upon any foe
Who crossed my path,
When I destroyed everyone I encountered
And seized all before me,
All twelve parts of my body were whole.
Thick-armed and stone-hearted,
A full-limbed, bold young warrior,
I made much blood flow across the plains;
Such was my stony courage and strength.
While my sovereign lived,
While I possessed my former strength,
Among all humankind,
He loaded the white musket.
From the hero’s fury,
The black earth, whose breast is hairy,
Stopped the shot only in its deepest layers.
When he raged in wrath,
The whole wide world stood watch;
The thick black earth below
Smoldered through its deepest layers
From my khan uncle’s fury.
When the providential hero lived,
Crimson steel took heads;
Against whoever provoked his wrath,
He ravaged the world and set it aflame.
He kindled the grassy lands
And set the meadows afire.
My exceedingly noble sultan uncle
Was truly a hero;
Among all humankind,
That peerless, keen-eyed eagle
Was truly a lion.
He broke through dead ends and opened roads;
My falcon uncle, my eagle,
Broke through on every side and opened roads,
And struck down all who opposed him.
He swept aside everyone he met,
And burned everyone he encountered.
Along the great road no host could overtake,
He made his bay horse dance;
Subduing everyone he encountered,
He made his assailants crawl.
He broke fortresses and took khans;
Against innumerable foes,
He raised dust such as no man had seen.
At the hero’s fury,
The enemies who grappled with him stood amazed.
When his fit of rage seized him,
He fiercely launched the turmoil.
He cut off the heads
Of the enemies who attacked him and subdued them;
He was truly a mighty mainstay.
Yesterday, on the plain of Jylgyndy,
Along broad Talas,
When my formidable lord lived,
Whenever restless, I would shoot mountain sheep,
Then turn back and lie at ease.
When the mighty hero lived,
I, poor wretch, would test my strength:
Setting them in rows, with my bow
I would shoot eighty in succession.
Such was my former nature,”
Said Külchoro, and thus
He spoke in verse of his former prowess
And the great conflicts,
And told of the mighty turmoil
That could never be healed.
Heroic Seytek heard his secrets
And readied himself like a hawk.
From the panther hero’s words,
Wisdom came to him from far away;
A sheathless sword was buckled on,
And your wretch blessed by the holy wanderer
Stepped forth, prepared to speak:
“My uncle Külchoro
Is the guardian above my head,
My fortune in heroic deeds.
From the traditions handed down,
And from questioning the wise,
I learned that assembled hosts stood together,
That he was an ember blazing like a minaret,
And throughout the whole wide world
There was none like my uncle.
He was a hero and a mainstay,
A lion surpassing all mankind.
He was one of those heroes
Who brought torment upon their foes in battle,
One of those souls who stirred
Great turmoil across the world.
His lashes were flame and his eyes embers;
No man was ever so fearsome!
When my uncle entered battle,
He burned forests into desert.
When he advanced, the enemy grieved;
His heroic, lionhearted prowess
Became known throughout the world.
The enemies who encountered him
Fell from their horses like severed sheaves.
When my uncle grew wrathful,
The people of the khagan fell.
He threw all who faced him into uproar,
And brought strife upon all he met.
He leveled even the soaring Ala-Too
With consummate skill;
He saved the Kyrgyz of Ala-Too from suffering
And made them a united people.
Building as he went, he made them homes;
Planting as he went, he made them orchards,
And guarded Talas as their homeland.
Among the peoples of the world, that noble soul
Made the renowned Choro a lion.
My uncle Semetey
Was perfect in every way;
If you looked within his heart,
It was broader than the face of the earth.
Such was my uncle,
Whose homeland was broad Talas,
Whose father was mighty, magnanimous Manas.
When I gathered together
The four corners of the earth,
When I subdued the whole wide world
And ruled it,
When I honed
The black-steel Zulpukor,
When I drove onward
All the peoples of the world,
Breaking ice to make a road
And bringing evildoers low,
Breaking rock to make a road
And bringing challengers low,
When I pursued all who fled
And let none escape,
When an enemy truly attacked,
If he grappled, I sent him on his final road
And dealt out punishment with my own hand.
No mortal dared face me;
No attacking enemy defeated me.
When I leveled my spear, it became flame;
When an enemy attacked, he ceased to exist.
He crossed the Urgench and opened a road;
He slaughtered heroic Kojo and brave Toltoy
And laid the two of them low.
He unleashed his fury fiercely
And slaughtered every warrior
Who boasted of his valor.
He broke through ravines and opened roads,
And laid hands upon the whole world.
A panther like a tiger,
My spearman uncle’s prowess
Was indeed beyond compare.
It was well known throughout the world
That his might was unsurpassed.
Plainly renowned and noble-browed,
His gray-maned valor stood apart.
Many called my tiger uncle Külchoro
A tiger among men,
Who devoured all he encountered.
When he tore men apart, he never had his fill of blood;
My uncle was a ravenous wolf.
My uncle, sustained by the sacred spirit,
Was called the people’s protector.
While strength remained across his broad back,
He made his gray-brown stallion dance;
Though countless myriads of foes came,
He hacked them down with his sword and subdued them,
Soaking his blade in blood.
Whoever provoked his wrath,
He killed and cast upon the ground.
Thick-armed and stone-hearted,
A full-limbed, bold young warrior,
He brought great calamity upon all he overtook.
He broke mountains and leveled the land.
Along the banks of Üch-Koshoy,
Where it meets the Talas,
On the flank lies Kan-Jailoo—
At the edge of Kan-Jailoo.
